previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, insulin-dependent diabetes, and recent coronary artery bypass grafting was admitted with chills and worsening right leg infection at the saphenous vein harvest site. Despite prior oral antibiotics, the infection progressed, with ultrasound revealing a fluid collection. He underwent two ultrasound-guided aspirations, yielding sanguinopurulent fluid that cultured E. coli. Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics were initiated and later tailored to vancomycin, ceftazidime, and metronidazole based on infectious disease guidance. Blood cultures remained negative. He continued scheduled hemodialysis and improved clinically, with resolution of fever and decreasing inflammation. He was discharged to rehabilitation to complete his antibiotic course, with instructions to monitor for fever, weight gain, and wound changes, and to follow up with his cardiologist and primary care provider.
